notes: SHIP v1.14.438 - THE RACK DETAIL COMES HOME, STEP 2 OF 4. WHAT THE WALK FOUND. Measured at .437: the rack-detail surface is a SECOND Build workspace. Both carry the current rack, the next action, OPEN AISLE, a rack elevation and phase state. The ONLY capabilities that existed solely on the detail were ASSIGN, QR and LOG NOTE - three things a technician could reach only by leaving the operational centre for a parallel screen doing the same job. Contract A7 says Build IS the operational centre, so they come here. THE MERGE IS STAGED IN FOUR STEPS AND THIS IS THE SECOND. Step 1 was the inventory - the step v1.14.431 skipped and paid a whole ship for. Step 2, this one, re-homes the three capabilities ADDITIVELY. Step 3 moves the MECH/PWR/NET/COMP/VAL dock so phase navigation lives with the phase work. Step 4 retires the detail as a destination, LAST, because the back-navigation restore path lands there and .437 only just made that landing coherent. Deleting it now would strand the thing that was fixed one ship ago. SAME DOORS, NOT COPIES. deploy_assignRack, deploy_generateRackQR and stripeRack_logNote each take deployId and rackId and are the canonical implementations; Build already knows both ids, which is the whole reason the detour existed and the whole reason it no longer needs to. Nothing was duplicated. CONTRACT 14 HELD DELIBERATELY. The three buttons are appended ONLY when a deployment AND a rack are resolved. With no rack there is nothing to assign, label or annotate, so they are ABSENT rather than present-and-dead - pinned by a test that boots with no deployment and asserts their absence. A SCOPE TRAP CAUGHT DURING THE BUILD, worth recording because it nearly shipped two dead buttons. The three doors are invoked through window lookup, and a check for top-level declarations reported only ONE of the three as global. That looked exactly like the IIFE-scope trap this file has been bitten by before - showToast, deploy_forge_master, statusOf - which would have made two of the three buttons throw on tap. It was a FALSE ALARM: the other two are declared async function, which a plain function grep does not match. The code was always right and the check was wrong. The reachability of all three is now pinned by test so that if any of them ever DOES become IIFE-scoped, the failure is a red spec rather than a dead control in an aisle. TESTS: new spec 27-rack-capabilities-in-build, five tests - the three are reachable from Build without displacing Scan or Log blocker, all three doors resolve at page scope, the buttons are absent with no rack resolved, the rack detail STILL works and STILL has its own buttons because this step is additive, and the new buttons fail loudly. 27: 5 passed. 26 plus 25 plus 02-build-forge: 23 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No CSS change, no renderer change - consolidation remains stopped per owner directive. DEVICE-VERIFY: open BUILD with an active rack. The action row should now read Scan, Log blocker, Assign, QR, Log note - five controls, all acting on the rack you are looking at, with no trip to a second screen. The rack detail is unchanged and still reachable; that is deliberate for this step.
